name: authowl-sdk-workspace

scripts.typecheck: pnpm -r --filter './packages/*' run typecheck && pnpm cli:e2e:typecheck && pnpm typecheck:storybook
scripts.test: pnpm release:contract:test && pnpm admin:generate:check && pnpm client-surface:check && pnpm dart-i18n:check && pnpm flutter:changelog:check && pnpm webhook:verify-docs && pnpm -r --filter './packages/*' run test
scripts.cli:e2e:fresh: pnpm build && pnpm cli:e2e:typecheck && vitest run --config vitest.tools.config.ts scripts/e2e/fresh-machine.test.ts

//pnpm.auditConfig: Three advisories in the Expo toolchain, ignored deliberately and scoped to
their exact GHSA ids. None of them is in anything we publish.
@authowl/expo declares expo-secure-store as a PEER dependency and passes
--external expo-secure-store to its build, so no artifact of ours bundles or
depends on it. Expo is present in this workspace only to satisfy that peer
for typecheck and build. A consumer of @authowl/expo has Expo already - it is
the reason they installed us - and these advisories live in their own
toolchain whether or not we exist.
GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr and GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq (image-size, ICNS and JXL/HEIF
denial of service) CANNOT be fixed: patched versions are <0.0.0, meaning no
release exists without the flaw, and 2.0.2 is the newest published. Reached
through metro at BUILD time, parsing an asset the developer added to their
own project. Revisit when image-size ships any fixed release.
Do not widen this list to whole packages or unpinned ranges. An advisory that
reaches a published artifact is a release blocker, not an entry here.
